questions: Resolve the exact Meta Muse Code product, exec JSON envelope and session protocol.
Verify cancellation, summary mode and resumable state without assuming flags from unrelated Muse CLIs.
decision: Use Muse explicit headless session/event contracts, enforce checkout isolation for parallel writers and reconcile cooperative cancellation before replacement workers.
code_observations: The repository has a dedicated Muse adapter and tests, rather than a generic command named Muse. The worker uses headless execution with configured model/effort options.
Meta documentation provides session-log controls and notes that child execution does not itself create an isolated checkout.
implementation_steps: Add version/help fixtures for Meta Muse Code and reject a same-named unrelated executable without the required command contract.
Separate JSONL progress/tool events from the final completion payload. Apply the shared bounded spool and schema validation.
Choose and document session-log retention for normal fresh workers; only add --no-session-log when supported and covered by a golden test.
Require explicit worktree/read-only controls for isolation. Never fall back from unsupported confinement to trust-workspace or approval bypass silently.
Normalize backend/usage identity and map failures through the same availability-versus-semantic distinction as other providers.
Require explicit isolation or serialization for Muse writers and verify the pinned source revision.
Wait for terminal cancellation evidence before replacement or cleanup; uncertain state remains recoverable.
Use exact headless session ids and versioned event schemas, never interactive resume in unattended execution.
proposed_acceptance_tests: A fixture for an unrelated muse executable is rejected before any task starts.
No-session-log and resume options are not combined incompatibly.
Two children sharing a checkout cannot be mistaken for isolated parallel writers.
Read-only summary and implementation command paths have different tested authority.
Large or malformed JSONL cannot cause unbounded memory or false completion.
A rejected isolation request cannot run in the shared checkout.
A cancelled child still writing blocks replacement until terminal reconciliation.
Interactive muse resume is not selected for a headless recovery.
An unrelated child log cannot be imported as task evidence.

alternatives.title: Shared checkout for all children
alternatives.tradeoff: Cheap startup; Write races and cancellation ambiguity. Read-only children only

alternatives.title: Isolated writers with terminal reconciliation
alternatives.tradeoff: Safe ownership and recovery; Merge and lifecycle overhead. Recommended

alternatives.title: Assume cancellation is immediate
alternatives.tradeoff: Fast replacement; Two writers can overlap. Reject

alternatives.title: Replace runner with session protocol
alternatives.tradeoff: Rich state; Provider-specific integration work. Optional after equivalence tests

cost_model: Use native parallelism only where independent validated outcomes offset setup and merge cost; avoid repeated full-journal ingestion.
unverified: Live Meta account permissions, model list, usage accounting and actual read-only enforcement remain unverified.
No Muse executable or session protocol was exercised. Cooperative cancellation behavior is documented, but actual timing and host capabilities need integration tests.

previous_decision: Qualify the exact Meta Muse Code executable and make session persistence, output envelopes and workspace isolation explicit.
revision_delta: The current Muse docs support per-child worktree isolation but explicitly describe cooperative cancellation. The revision adds cancellation-acknowledgement and base-revision evidence instead of assuming child termination.
decision_analysis: Default subagents can share the lead checkout. Parallel write scopes need explicit isolation or serialization, and an isolation request that cannot be honored must not fall back silently. Pin source revision and pass only relevant changes; checkout separation alone does not prevent incompatible edits to the same contract.

A cancel request is not proof that the child stopped. A worker may finish a write before reaching a cancellation checkpoint. Require terminal status and process/lease reconciliation before starting a replacement writer or deleting its workspace. Uncertain cancellation preserves the plan and evidence.

Headless sessions and interactive resume commands are separate surfaces. Use documented headless exec with an exact session id for any permitted resume, not the interactive UI. The versioned schema/session protocol can be an optional adapter boundary, but a stable schema version still needs event, usage and terminal-outcome fixtures.

Muse session logs and child journals can contain the full execution context. Keep them outside normal worker prompts and outside release artifacts. Retain only non-secret identity and bounded evidence references in the shared ledger, with an explicit policy for provider-created logs beyond the plan directory.
